questions.text: When unexposed films are stored in accepted safety shipping containers, what aggregate volume triggers automatic fire extinguishing systems?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: More than 14.00 cu.m. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.

questions.text: What shelving capacity for individual packages not in accepted safety shipping containers triggers automatic fire extinguishing systems?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: More than 1.40 cu.m. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.

questions.text: How many film negatives may be kept in one heavy Manila envelope?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Not more than twelve films. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: The 450 kg aggregate threshold is the critical vault trigger in Sec. 1401. A facility may use multiple cabinets, each within the 110 kg individual limit, up to but not exceeding 450 kg total without requiring vault construction. At 450 kg and above, the collective fire load exceeds cabinet containment capacity, requiring vault-standard construction with 4-hour fire-resistive doors.

questions.text: Which envelope type is prohibited for film negatives?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Expanding envelopes. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.

questions.text: What is the maximum film weight allowed in any single cabinet?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 110 kg. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.

questions.text: When stored film exceeds what weight must it be placed in a vented vault, detached structure, or roof vault?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 450 kg. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.

questions.text: What fire-resistive construction is required for vault door openings?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Four-hour fire-resistive construction. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: Under the DENSE mnemonic (Dental, Establishments manufacturing, Neat original packages, Safety film, Enclosures/motion picture booths), amateur roll film in original packages below 1.40 cu.m, dental X-ray film, and safety film (identified by edge marking) are all exempt. Medical X-ray film negatives stored on open shelving at 2.50 cu.m — well above the 1.40 cu.m open shelving threshold and not in original packaging — are fully subject to Sec. 1401 requirements.

questions.text: What minimum distance must films be kept from steam pipes, chimneys, or other heat sources?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 600 mm. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.

questions.text: What first-aid firefighting provision is specified for photographic and x-ray film storage?

options.text: Types using water or water solutions

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Types using water or water solutions. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: Sec. 1401 is explicit: when total film storage exceeds 450 kg, a vented storage vault is required, and vault door openings must be of 4-hour fire-resistive construction. The vault must be vented (to prevent buildup of decomposition gases that precede ignition) and vault doors must be kept closed except when in use — a propped-open 4-hour door provides zero protection. This requirement applies at any mass above 450 kg aggregate.

All film stored near heat sources

questions.explanation: Sec. 1401 explicitly limits each Manila envelope to a maximum of 12 film negatives. This compartmentalizes the fuel load so that a single envelope fire cannot grow into a larger mass fire. The prohibition on expanding (accordion-style) envelopes is absolute — they can be overfilled beyond 12 films without visible indication.

questions.rationale: Correct answer: More than 14.00 cu.m. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: The 4-hour rating is the highest in the PD 1096 system — it signals that X-ray film vaults are among the most hazardous occupancy-related storage applications addressed by the Code. The keep-closed requirement is operationally mandatory, not a recommendation.

questions.text: What shelving capacity for individual packages not in accepted safety shipping containers triggers automatic fire extinguishing systems?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: More than 1.40 cu.m. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: Modern X-ray film (acetate or polyester base) is technically safety film and qualifies for the exemption. However, pre-1960s archival radiology collections may contain cellulose nitrate film that is NOT exempt. Architects designing archives must verify the film stock type before applying exemptions.

questions.explanation: The capacity-based trigger (not stock-based) is an often-missed detail. A 2.00 cu.m shelf holding only 0.80 cu.m of film on any given day still triggers the suppression requirement because its capacity exceeds 1.40 cu.m.

questions.text: What is the maximum film weight allowed in any single cabinet?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 110 kg. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: The 10:1 ratio between containerized (14.00 cu.m) and open-shelving (1.40 cu.m) thresholds is the most testable quantitative relationship in Rule XIV. Safety shipping containers are passive fire protection — remove them, and the threshold drops by 90%.

questions.text: When stored film exceeds what weight must it be placed in a vented vault, detached structure, or roof vault?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: 450 kg. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: The prohibition on portable extension cord lights is absolute. This is the most commonly violated provision in practice — a portable work light left on a shelf during after-hours access is a direct code violation regardless of its wattage or condition.

questions.text: What fire-resistive construction is required for vault door openings?
questions.rationale: Correct answer: Four-hour fire-resistive construction. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1401.
questions.explanation: This question requires applying three independent thresholds simultaneously: 110 kg per cabinet (satisfied), 450 kg aggregate vault trigger (not reached), and 1.40 cu.m open shelving capacity trigger (exceeded). Only the open shelving requirement is violated.
